title: Two Players, Two Scores
statement: Robin and Sasha play a game in rounds, and both start with $0$ points. Every round has exactly one winner and one loser, with no draws. The winner of a round gains $5$ points and the loser of that round gains $2$ points. At the end of the game, Robin has $51$ points and Sasha has $33$ points. How many rounds did Robin win?
hints: Look at the total number of points the two players receive together in a single round. Does that total depend on who wins the round?

Use algebra: let Robin win $r$ rounds and Sasha win $s$ rounds, and write one equation for each player's final score. Adding the two equations is useful because $r$ and $s$ then have the same coefficient, which gives the total number of rounds.

The two final scores add up to $84$, and each round contributes $7$ points to this total, so there were $12$ rounds. Robin gains at least $2$ points in every round and gains $3$ extra in each round Robin wins. Compare this with Robin's $51$ points.
solution: Let Robin win $r$ rounds and Sasha win $s$ rounds. Every round has exactly one winner, so the total number of rounds is $r + s$. Robin gains $5$ points for each of the $r$ wins and $2$ points for each of the $s$ losses, and the same reasoning applies to Sasha. Therefore $$5r + 2s = 51 \quad \text{and} \quad 2r + 5s = 33.$$ Adding these two equations gives $7(r + s) = 84$, so $r + s = 12$. This matches the fact that the two players together gain $5 + 2 = 7$ points in every round, whoever wins it. There were therefore $12$ rounds. Now split Robin's score into two parts. Robin gains at least $2$ points in each of the $12$ rounds, which makes $2 \cdot 12 = 24$ points, and each round Robin wins gives $5 - 2 = 3$ points more. In symbols, $5r + 2s = 2(r + s) + 3r$, so $24 + 3r = 51$. This gives $3r = 27$, so $r = 9$. As a check, $r = 9$ and $s = 3$ give Robin $5 \cdot 9 + 2 \cdot 3 = 51$ points and Sasha $2 \cdot 9 + 5 \cdot 3 = 33$ points, as required. The answer is $9$. Why this works. linear-combination-of-equations, linear-system-solving: adding the two score equations gives the number of rounds because every round adds the same total of $7$ points, and Robin's equation then has only one unknown left.
